title: Fractographical characterization of hot pressed and pressureless sintered AlN-doped ZrB2-SiC composites

nodes.label: ZrB2-SiC ultra-high-temperature ceramics need full densification without costly high-pressure hot pressing
How AlN doping changes the interfacial phases and the fracture mode of ZrB2-SiC is uncharacterised
AlN should scavenge the B2O3 surface oxide and create a low-melting liquid that drives liquid-phase sintering
ZrB2-30 vol% SiC with 4 wt% phenolic resin binder pyrolysing to 1.6 wt% carbon

attrs.reason: standard UHTC composite; resin carbon also acts as sintering aid

nodes.label: AlN added to the ZrB2-SiC base as oxygen-scavenging sintering aid
AlN content 0, 1, 3, 5 wt% crossed with two consolidation routes (HP vs PS)
Hot pressing at 1900 C under 10 MPa for 2 h
Pressureless sintering at 1900 C for 2 h in 5e-2 Pa vacuum
AlN is fully consumed: HP5 holds BN and graphite, PS5 holds Al2OC; no AlN or Al2O3 reflections remain
Nano-scale Al-rich, N- and B-bearing glassy layers and a multilayer carbon band wet the ZrB2/SiC boundaries
Hot-pressed composites reach 100% relative density at 1 and 5 wt% AlN, from 97.5% undoped
Pressureless-sintered porosity grows with AlN: relative density falls 85.5 -> 70.0%
Hot-pressed fracture is dominantly transgranular; pressureless samples fail intergranularly at necks
Vickers hardness peaks at 20.3 GPa for HP1 and falls to 6.8 GPa for PS5
Applied pressure expels gaseous products and forces the aluminosilicate liquid into pores, completing densification
Without pressure the CO and B2O3 vapour released by the same reactions is trapped, outweighing the extra necking AlN provides
AlN is a useful sintering aid only under pressure; 1 wt% under hot pressing is the optimum, and AlN is counterproductive for pressureless sintering
Fractography plus XRD/EDS/TEM ties full density and transgranular fracture in HP to an AlN-derived interfacial liquid, and PS porosity to trapped gas
HP relative density stays >=97.5% and reaches 100% at 1 and 5 wt% AlN

notes: Two-branch spine: the same AlN chemistry (m9) feeds a pressure branch (LPS -> full density -> transgranular fracture) and a pressureless control branch (trapped CO/B2O3 -> porosity -> intergranular failure), meeting at the hardness node m14. Packet figure ids are offset from the paper: packet F5/F6/F7 carry paper Figs 6/7/8 and paper Fig. 5 is absent from the record; panel ids follow the packet. Numbers in o1/o2/o3 are read off F2a/F2b, not from the MatMech block, which quotes PS1 at ~92% relative density against the panel's 78.3%. The text places the N- and B-bearing EDS spectrum in Fig. 6b, but the image file puts it in panel (a) (o9). Lost: the HP3/PS3 intermediate compositions, Table 2 sample coding, and the full reaction thermodynamics.

changes: o9: label said the HP5 interfacial EDS is 'Al-dominated'. Re-read against the keV axis, Zr Lalpha is the largest peak (~55) and Al (~22) is only the strongest light-element line. Label corrected, image_support lowered shown -> partial, image_note now gives the peak heights and keeps the Fig. 6b/panel (a) placement defect.
a1: image_note extended - the ~26 deg reflection carries a ZrB2 marker as well as the graphite and BN markers, which strengthens the audit (that peak identifies neither interfacial phase).

m17 (DSC/design_guidance) taken off the spine. The paper's headline is the fractographic characterization, not the guidance, so by the r04 spine rule only DSC/conclusion (m18) belongs on it. Spine 18 -> 17; added m13 -> m18 supports so the fracture-mode branch still reaches the conclusion.

panel_checks.note: F2a PS series reads 85.5, 78.3, 70.6, 70.0% at 0/1/3/5 wt%, exactly as the node states, and the HP series 97.5/100/99.3/100. The node's flag that the MatMech summary quotes PS1 at ~92% is correct: the panel contradicts it.

Panel id right (F5a = paper Fig. 6a, HP5, the arrowed layered band and its EDS) but the panel does not show the claim as it was stated: Zr Lalpha at ~2.05 keV is the largest peak (~55 counts), not Al (~22). No other panel supports 'Al-dominated' - F5b (PS5) is more Zr-dominated still - so no correct_id; the node has been corrected.
Measured on the crop: the 100 nm bar is 91 px, the bright interfacial band is 20-43 px vertically on a boundary inclined ~26 deg, i.e. 20-43 nm perpendicular. The node's '~20-40 nm' is right.

Extra check. F4a point-A EDS is Si-dominated (~2300) with a Zr doublet (~350/250) and Al, B, C, N at or near noise, exactly as the node and its image_note state; image_support=partial against the text's 'mainly boron, carbon, silicon and zirconium' is fair.
Extra check. F6b carries Al2OC markers at ~33, ~59 and ~63.5 deg and no graphite marker; F6a has graphite and BN but no Al2OC. The ~33 deg Al2OC marker does sit on a peak that also carries ZrB2.

review.audit_summary: 3 audits (a1, a2, lim1) plus one DSC/comparison, all within budget and all load-bearing. a1 and lim1 both bear on m10, the interfacial-phase claim, which is the paper's weakest link: it rests on point EDS and on single weak XRD peaks that coincide with a ZrB2 reflection. Both are stated as 'the figure does not resolve it', not as contradiction, which is the right reading. a2 is a fair proportionality audit (the undoped HP sample is already 97.5% dense, so AlN buys at most 2.5 points under pressure) and correctly qualifies m15 as well as m11. The one genuine figure-vs-text conflict in this paper sits on image_support (o6 partial, o9 partial) rather than in an extra node, as the audit budget intends.
